ROLE: observer
You review the results of an incident investigation. Write a short summary of what the latest results show, then update the list of hypotheses (at most 4, most likely first).

Root-cause categories:
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Each hypothesis has root_cause_category (one of the categories), rationale, and supporting_evidence_ids (only IDs that appear in the evidence below).

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"summary": "...", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "disk_full", "rationale": "...", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0123"]}]}

Alert: inventory-service: p99 latency above 1000ms for 5 minutes (since 19:43 UTC)
Alerting service: inventory
Alert time: 2026-05-13T19:43:00Z
Data available from 2026-05-13T18:00:00Z to 2026-05-13T21:00:00Z

Evidence so far (the latest results are steps 4 onwards):
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-13T20:30:00Z", "metric": "latency_p99_ms", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-05-13T19:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check latency evolution for inventory service.)
  Result: M-024: Change detected at 2026-05-13T19:20:00Z: mean 122.84 before, 3643.03 after (1008.5 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-024] inventory.latency_p99_ms from 2026-05-13T19:00:00Z to 2026-05-13T20:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=109.63 max=5167.61 mean=2901.94 last=5152.33; mean=2901.94. Change detected at 2026-05-13T19:20:00Z: mean 122.84 before, 3643.03 after (1008.5 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-13T19:20:00Z = 109.63 (first point after the change); 2026-05-13T19:20:00Z = 109.63 (lowest); 2026-05-13T19:55:00Z = 5167.61 (peak); 2026-05-13T20:30:00Z = 5152.33 (last).
Step 2: metrics_query {"end": "2026-05-13T20:30:00Z", "metric": "db_pool_in_use_pct", "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-05-13T19:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check database connection pool usage for inventory service.)
  Result: M-021: Change detected at 2026-05-13T19:30:00Z: mean 30.7 before, 64.76 after (15.5 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-021] inventory.db_pool_in_use_pct from 2026-05-13T19:00:00Z to 2026-05-13T20:30:00Z (19 points, 5-minute steps): min=27.2 max=78.77 mean=54 last=77.41; mean=54. Change detected at 2026-05-13T19:30:00Z: mean 30.7 before, 64.76 after (15.5 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-05-13T19:10:00Z = 27.2 (lowest); 2026-05-13T19:30:00Z = 37.85 (first point after the change); 2026-05-13T20:25:00Z = 78.77 (peak); 2026-05-13T20:30:00Z = 77.41 (last).
Step 3: log_search {"end": "2026-05-13T19:45:00Z", "limit": 30, "service": "inventory", "start": "2026-05-13T19:35:00Z"} (asked because: Search for warnings or errors in inventory logs around the incident start time.)
  Result: 13 matching log lines.
  [L-0292] 2026-05-13T19:37:35Z inventory INFO metrics scrape served bytes=37905
  [L-0300] 2026-05-13T19:40:23Z inventory WARN slow query took 9269ms: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_ref = $1 rows_examined=4213877
  [L-0302] 2026-05-13T19:41:12Z inventory WARN query plan: Seq Scan on orders (rows=4213877) filter=(customer_ref = $1) no usable index
  [L-0304] 2026-05-13T19:41:17Z inventory INFO stock level query sku=SKU-1217 on_hand=179
  [L-0305] 2026-05-13T19:41:20Z inventory WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0306] 2026-05-13T19:41:23Z inventory WARN slow request took 453ms path=/api/v1/stock/bulk
  [L-0310] 2026-05-13T19:42:05Z inventory ERROR request failed status=502 path=/api/v1/cart request_id=req-9d60889f
  [L-0312] 2026-05-13T19:42:11Z inventory WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0315] 2026-05-13T19:43:08Z inventory ERROR request failed status=500 path=/api/v1/cart request_id=req-48d0ce77 duration_ms=17014
  [L-0316] 2026-05-13T19:43:17Z inventory WARN request error rate above SLO window=5m
  [L-0318] 2026-05-13T19:43:48Z inventory ERROR upstream returned 503 for /api/v1/cart request_id=req-d93e67f5
  [L-0320] 2026-05-13T19:44:18Z inventory ERROR upstream returned 503 for /api/v1/cart request_id=req-a732ccbd
  [L-0322] 2026-05-13T19:44:38Z inventory ERROR upstream returned 503 for /api/v1/cart request_id=req-0886da73
Step 4: runbook_retrieve {"query": "slow query missing index database optimization"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook guidance and mitigation steps for slow queries and missing indexes.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-03-3 (similarity 0.71).
  [R-03-3] Slow query or missing index - How to confirm (similarity 0.71): Search the logs for slow query warnings and for query plans showing a full scan of a large table. Check whether a schema migration recently dropped or changed an index. The slowness is present at normal traffic, and a single query taking several seconds is the signature, rather than short queries waiting for a connection.
  [R-03-7] Slow query or missing index - Escalation (similarity 0.70): Talk to the database team before building an index on a very large table during peak hours, since the build itself adds load and can take a long time to finish.
  [R-03-5] Slow query or missing index - Mitigation (similarity 0.70): Recreate the missing index using a concurrent build so writes are not blocked, then refresh the table statistics. As a stopgap, cancel the long-running queries and add a statement timeout. Revert the migration that removed the index if one is found.

Previous hypotheses:
- slow_query_missing_index: Logs show a slow query warning explicitly noting a sequential scan on the orders table with no usable index and examining over 4 million rows. (evidence: L-0300, L-0302)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: Database connection pool usage increased significantly starting around 19:30 UTC, likely secondary to slow queries holding onto connections. (evidence: M-021)

response: {"summary": "Log search and runbook retrieval confirm that the inventory service is experiencing performance degradation due to a slow query performing a sequential scan without a usable index on the orders table, leading to high latency and secondary database pool pressure.", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "slow_query_missing_index", "rationale": "Logs explicitly show a slow query warning with a sequential scan on the orders table examining over 4 million rows with no usable index, matching runbook signatures.", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0300", "L-0302", "R-03-3"]}, {"root_cause_category": "db_connection_pool_exhaustion", "rationale": "Database connection pool usage increased significantly following the onset of slow queries holding connections.", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["M-021"]}]}
